criteria.check: Booked only: convert() leaves out Status=Pending and counts it once per id, takes off any id later seen booked (pending_ids, pending -= len(pending_ids & first.keys())), and refuses any other status. GBP only: _money refuses a non-GBP amount or balance; a pending non-GBP line is left out before currency is read. Provider ids: _id keeps TransactionId as the line id (per_line_balances.statement.golden T1..T5; test_provider_ids_are_the_line_ids). Paged repeats: kept once when the content is equal, refused when it differs. Rebuilt balance: the opening comes from the first per-line balance, or from --statement-balance/--at (checked against the per-line balances when both exist), and contract.walk (src/cma/importers/contract.py:81-90) checks every per-line balance against the walked one, so a break anywhere is refused. verify-257 major fixed: _order checks a single-line group against `before` (openbanking.py:297-299), so _first_order cannot take a start that a later single balanced line contradicts. I traced _first_order and convert: walked after group k equals start + totals[k], the cache keys match, the pinned starts from a fully balanced later group are exhaustive, and a later group that cannot be ordered from the fixed balance is refused at that group. The runner's contracts tier ran every test_import_openbanking test and all passed (contracts-4.log, 119 lines, none failed), including the verify-257 regressions at lines 223-246.

findings.claim: The claim says hostile JSON (100k nested brackets) and NaN are refused, not crashed. No runner-run test proves this: nothing in test_import_openbanking.py feeds NaN, Infinity or deep nesting, and the only proof is a producer-run python -c. The code path (_scanner's parse_constant raising ValueError, and _pages catching ValueError and RecursionError) looks right, but the claim is unproven.
findings.repro: grep -n 'NaN\|nested\|deep' tests/test_import_openbanking.py finds only copy.deepcopy. Add cases such as b'{"Data": {"Transaction": [{"Amount": NaN}]}}' and b'[' * 100000 to test_a_file_that_is_not_an_obie_transactions_response_is_refused.

findings.claim: Lines are sorted by the date as the bank wrote it before the UTC moment. In a file that mixes UTC 'Z' and +01:00 offsets near midnight, that sort can put two lines in the wrong time order. A valid chain whose balances follow the true order is then refused as not following. This is narrow; a single bank normally writes one offset convention.
findings.repro: Two booked lines with balances: X at 2026-04-01T23:30:00Z (date 04-01) and Y at 2026-04-02T00:15:00+01:00 (=04-01T23:15Z, date 04-02), with Y booked first so Y.balance + X.amount == X.balance. The sort puts X before Y, and contract.walk refuses at Y's line.
